dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: It's too bad Cater isn't here! If he was, he could enjoy this with us too!

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Even if Cater was here, you still wouldn't be allowed to drink any more Fonta today.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Awww... But Cater said, you have to share with others to be even more happy!

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: I'm sure Cater also said not to have too much sugar and to brush your teeth after eating.

dialogues.speaker: Lanoire
dialogues.text: Oh... He did mention that...

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: How's your trip been, kid? Why not take a load off and put your feet up for a bit?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks. How are Hero and the others?

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Well, they're fine — by which I mean they're always making me worry. What's new?

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: At least they're alive and kicking, which means they're healthy. That's always a good thing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks. Has your daughter returned home?

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Hmph. Don't even talk about it.

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: That stubborn girl... I don't think she ever intends to come back.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks. But I'll be going now.

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Alright. Now, don't be a hero if you run into any trouble on your journey. Look after yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: It's getting late. You should get some rest, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Agnes...

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: If she hadn't been so stubborn... *sigh* It's my fault, I was the one who was too stubborn. I'm a stone-hearted old fool.

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: But according to Lanoire, she smiled at everyone, even until the very end...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Lanoire...

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: That child... She's just like her mother — spirited and independent.

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Children grow up so quickly. What can I say? I just hope that she can live the life she wants. Health and happiness are more important than anything else.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night.

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Good night, children. Sweet dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Phew, that was close...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: *sigh* I didn't think that there would be any hilichurls that dared to attack people so close to the Court of Fontaine. I don't know what I'd have done if Lanoire was hurt. But thanks to you...

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: I was of a mind to not let her run around again. But if I did that, how different would life here be from life in the Fortress of Meropide?

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: I suppose I'll just keep her company more often, so that if anything happens, she'll at least have some adult to rely on.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Earnshaw
dialogues.text: Bye, take care! Don't have your loved ones worrying about you, alright?
